theory.intro: A parameter supplies both coordinates of a point.
facts: Use the same value of $t$ in $x(t)$ and $y(t)$.
Changing $t$ traces the curve, but the point may reverse direction and retrace part of it.
Different parametrisations can trace the same curve.
A restricted parameter interval may trace only a segment or arc.

workedExamples.question_text: For $x=2t+2,\ y=t-2$, find the point when $t=3$.
For $x=4t,\ y=2t^{2}$, find the point when $t=-3$. Explain what this value of $t$ determines.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Use the same value of $t$ in both equations.
$\begin{align*}x&=4(-3)\\&=-12\end{align*}$
$\begin{align*}y&=2(-3)^{2}\\&=18\end{align*}$
The value $t=-3$ determines one ordered pair, $(-12,18)$.

workedExamples.question_text: For $x=3t,\ y=t^{2}$, find the value of $t$ that gives the point $(12,16)$.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Use the $x$-coordinate to find $t$.
$\begin{align*}3t&=12\\t&=4\end{align*}$
Check the same parameter in the other equation: $y=4^{2}=16$.
The point occurs when $t=4$.

workedExamples.question_text: For $x=3+t,\ y=4-2t^{2}$ with $-2\le t\le0$, find the range of $x$.
workedExamples.solution_text:
$\begin{align*}x(-2)&=3+(-2)=1\\x(0)&=3+0=3\end{align*}$
Since $x=3+t$ increases throughout the parameter interval, its range is $[1,3]$. Both endpoints are included.

workedExamples.question_text: For $x=7-t^{2},\ y=t^{2}-5$, where $t$ is real, find the restriction on $x$.
workedExamples.solution_text:
For real $t$, $t^{2}\ge0$, so $x=7-t^{2}\le7$.
Equality occurs when $t=0$. Every smaller value is possible because $t^{2}$ can take any nonnegative value.
The restriction is $x\le7$.

For $x=2t+2,\ y=t-2$, find the point when $t=3$.
For $x=2t+5,\ y=t-2$, what does one value of $t$ determine?
foundation.solution_text:
Substitute the same parameter into both equations.
$\text{one ordered pair }(x,y)$
